scope: Windows internal-speaker DEFAULT-owner overlap with explicit NOTIFICATION, plus isolated NOTIFICATION falsification

overlap_default_then_alerts.result: The alert was classified as NOTIFICATION by qcaudminiport, but no fresh qcadcm render-family selection occurred while the already-live DEFAULT endpoint graph remained active.

isolated_alerts_after_audio_engine_cold_.result: The same explicit Alerts class selects the NOTIFICATION lower family when it starts from an idle/cold audio-engine lifetime.

interpretation.directly_observed: DEFAULT-first overlap keeps the existing lower qcadcm family selection even though the later stream is classified NOTIFICATION.
interpretation.strong_inference: Windows processing mode is an endpoint/audio-engine graph-lifetime choice rather than an independently opened AudioReach family per simultaneously mixed client stream.
interpretation.not_yet_proven: The reciprocal NOTIFICATION-first then DEFAULT overlap/switchover behavior. Do not generalize the one-way result to a universal first-stream-wins rule yet.

tooling_notes: qcadcm and QCAUD PnP images were recovered through !drvobj and PE AddressOfEntryPoint because they were not exposed through normal lm enumeration in this session.
The successful mode capture mechanism is ba e1, matching the earlier reviewed ARM64 capture. Software bp/bu was not a valid substitute here.

Repeated qcadcm selector hardware trapping can produce unmatched ARM64 single-step stops on unrelated ACDB calls; future selector captures should be cold, bounded, and avoid automatic pointer dereferences.
A qualifying 0x5aa34 OOB hook did not fire in these lifecycle tests; that absence is not used as the primary graph-lifetime conclusion.
